name: Lapis-Caldera
description: Lapis-Caldera is a world of deep blue fire, its magma colored by exotic mineral compounds that burn in shades of cobalt and ultramarine rather than the expected reds and golds. Massive calderas pock the surface like craters, each one a cauldron of blue-white lava bordered by walls of dark volcanic glass. The canyon systems between calderas run with rivers of acid condensate, their banks encrusted with crystallized sulfate compounds in vivid yellow and white.

The atmosphere is a choking mix of sulfur compounds and metalite particulates that tint the sky a permanent deep indigo. Acid rain falls in sheets across the equatorial regions, dissolving exposed rock and rebuilding it in strange, corroded formations. The beauty of the blue magma is matched by its lethality; the compounds that give it color are profoundly toxic to carbon-based life.

Lapis-Caldera's exotic matter deposits were discovered by an automated survey probe that was subsequently lost to a volcanic event. The deposits appear to form in the unique chemical conditions of the blue calderas, a synthesis process that has never been observed elsewhere. Theoretical physicists consider the planet a natural laboratory for exotic matter formation, but accessing the deposits requires surviving conditions that destroy conventional equipment within hours.

The exotic matter alone makes Lapis-Caldera one of the most strategically valuable uninhabitable worlds in known space. Multiple governments and corporations have filed competing claims, none of which have been adjudicated. Robotic extraction attempts have achieved limited success, but the corrosive atmosphere degrades machinery faster than it can be replaced. The blue fires burn on, indifferent to the ambitions of those who covet what they produce.
